decisions.justification: Q1 asked what to do when a target exists, and the user chose to abort the entire run, report every conflict, and never overwrite.
Q5 and Q9 asked about rollback for execution-time failures and its realistic guarantee boundary; the user required best-effort rollback with explicit rollback-failure reporting.
Q7 addressed exact source-to-same-name mappings, but nobody decided whether files already matching the overall target naming scheme should be included in the rename set.
Q2 explicitly asked whether rename chains should be rejected, and the user chose the strict rule that rejects them.
The session never asked what a second identical invocation does; Q18 only covered already-produced empty or all-exact-no-op plans.
Q12 asked how case-only names should behave on case-insensitive filesystems, and the user chose to treat them as clashes.
Q3, Q4, Q10, Q15, Q16, Q17, and Q19 settled output streams, diagnostic content and ordering, and the non-zero status.
The session neither asked whether preview or confirmation belonged in the fix nor settled whether safety could depend on operator review.

mustPreserveKept: user-facing output on stdout and diagnostics on stderr

notes: The session thoroughly elicited collision, rollback, and diagnostic behavior, and the implementation visibly attempts those choices. It missed self-inclusion, repeat-run idempotency, and preview policy, while the case-insensitive handling only covers Windows; moreover, the check-then-rename race can still overwrite a newly appeared target and rollback failure can leave changes behind, so neither absolute acceptance guarantee is met.
